crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Drafting Proposal Responses
children.blurb: Drafting Proposal Responses covers the use of AI agents to assemble, tailor, and review answers to requests for proposals, requests for information, due diligence questionnaires, and security questionnaires in financial services.

children.name: Agent Negotiation in Over-the-Counter Markets
children.blurb: Agent negotiation in over the counter markets covers software agents that represent buyers, sellers, dealers, or clients in bilateral and voice or chat based trading of instruments not listed on exchanges, such as swaps, bonds, FX forwards, and structured notes.

children.name: Investment Committee Memos
children.blurb: Investment committee memos are the formal documents that present a proposed investment to the committee that approves, rejects, or conditions it.

children.name: Keeping Comparable Company Sets Current
children.blurb: Keeping comparable company sets current means maintaining a peer group used for valuation, relative performance, and sector benchmarking as the underlying companies change.

children.name: Automating Trade Settlement
children.blurb: Automating trade settlement covers the post-trade steps that turn an executed trade into a final transfer of cash and securities, including trade enrichment, matching, confirmation, clearing, settlement instruction generation, reconciliation, and fails management.

sections.body: Agent workflows in finance are the places where language models and automated agents are wired into the ordinary paperwork and messaging of deal making. In practice this means drafting responses to requests for proposals, running or assisting negotiations in over the counter markets, assembling investment committee memos, refreshing comparable company sets, and pushing trades through settlement. The work is less about predicting markets and more about moving documents, checking figures and keeping counterparties in sync. A tracked universe of 514 company pages and 394 merger and acquisition filings gives these workflows a steady supply of real material to draft from and reconcile against.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Drafting and memo assembly are the most mature parts, because the output is text that a human reviews before it leaves the building. Negotiation agents are further behind, since over the counter terms are private, relationship driven and rarely written down in a form a model can learn from. Settlement automation is constrained by legacy systems and by the fact that a wrong instruction moves real money, so agents tend to prepare and check rather than execute. The honest limits are consistent across all five areas: models are good at retrieval, formatting and first drafts, and weak at accountability, novel terms and anything requiring a signature. Nothing here removes the need for a human who owns the decision.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages run roughly in the order a deal moves. Drafting Proposal Responses covers the front end, turning a client request into a structured answer, while Agent Negotiation in Over the Counter Markets takes on the messier back and forth of terms and quotes. Investment Committee Memos sits in the middle, where the reasoning and the numbers have to be assembled into something a committee can act on, and Keeping Comparable Company Sets Current is the maintenance job that keeps those numbers honest over time. Automating Trade Settlement closes the loop on the operational side, where the agreed trade has to be confirmed and recorded. A reader new to the area should start with the drafting page, and anyone focused on controls should go straight to settlement.
